title: Net 1 and Net 365 are exact to the day
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: Two customers on the shop's own terms due 1 day and 365 days after the invoice date have work orders ready to invoice.
  • You are an Admin user working at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Customers {Customer-A} and {Customer-B} hold the shop's own terms {Term-A} (due 1 day after the invoice date) and {Term-B} (due 365 days after).
    For example: the customers are ZZAUTOTEST DATA-10 A and B, {Term-A} is ZZAUTOTEST DATA-10 N1 and {Term-B} is ZZAUTOTEST DATA-10 N365.
  • Work orders {Work-order-1} for {Customer-A} and {Work-order-2} for {Customer-B} are complete and ready to invoice.
    For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-15440 and {Work-order-2} is S2-15441.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Open {Work-order-1}'s Finance tab.
  2. Set Invoice Date to Oct 31, 2026.
  3. Set Invoice Date to Dec 31, 2026.
  4. Open {Work-order-2}'s Finance tab.
  5. Set Invoice Date to Oct 5, 2026.
  6. Set Invoice Date to Feb 1, 2028.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the invoice preview shows.
  • Step 2: the Due date reads Nov 1, 2026 (Oct 31 + 1 day).
  • Step 3: the Due date reads Jan 1, 2027 (Dec 31 + 1 day).
  • Step 4: the invoice preview shows.
  • Step 5: the Due date reads Oct 5, 2027 (365 days; February 2027 has 28 days, so a year is exactly 365).
  • Step 6: the Due date reads Jan 31, 2029 (2028 has 366 days, so 365 days falls one day short of Feb 1).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates)

  • S7-R1: “A Net term (standard or the shop's own) is due that many days after the invoice date: an invoice dated Oct 5 on Net 30 is due Nov 4; on a shop's "Net 10" it is due Oct 15.”
  • Key Decisions: “Net terms run from 1 to 365 days.”
